findings.sentence: Given the interaction between Stimulus Type and Study Condition, we next determined whether the testing effect itself differed by stimulus type, by comparing the magnitude of the difference between restudy and retrieval practice for abstract versus meaningful, which was not significant, t(51) = 0.083, p = 0.93.

papers.title: The effects of oral versus written knowledge task prompt delivery in medical device usability testing
papers.summary: We found 17 t-tests and/or F-tests where effect sizes are not reported. Check these tests in the table below, and consider adding effect sizes.

findings.sentence: Written KTs yielded higher accuracy than Oral KTs, F(1, 36) = 6.44, p = .016, partial 𝜂² = .152.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between Written and Oral prompts did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 0.60, p = .443, partial 𝜂² = .016.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Participants consulted the IFU more frequently under Written than Oral KT prompts, F(1, 36) = 6.59, p = .015, partial 𝜂² = .155.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between Written and Oral KTs did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 0.07, p = .795, partial 𝜂² = .002.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Participants took longer to begin responding under Written than Oral KT prompts, F(1, 36) = 6.01, p = .019, partial 𝜂² = .143.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between the Written and Oral groups did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 3.39, p = .074, partial 𝜂² = .086.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The duration of participants' verbal responses did not statistically differ between Written and Oral KT prompts, F(1, 36) = 0.01, p = .908, partial 𝜂² < .001.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between the Written and Oral groups did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 0.33, p = .570, partial 𝜂² = .009.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Participants spent more time completing each KT under Written than Oral prompts, F(1, 36) = 5.16, p = .029, partial 𝜂² = .125.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between the Written and Oral groups did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 0.69, p = .411, partial 𝜂² = .019.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Participants spent more total time completing the 10-KT blocks under Written than Oral prompts, F(1, 30) = 11.60, p = .002, partial 𝜂² = .279.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between the Written and Oral groups did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 30) = 2.33, p = .137, partial 𝜂² = .072.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Participants in the Written Group yielded fewer moderator interventions than those in the Oral Group, F(1, 36) = 9.90, p = .003, partial 𝜂² = .216.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The difference between the Written and Oral groups did not statistically differ by device, F(1, 36) = 0.11, p = .740, partial 𝜂² = .003.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: State anxiety did not clearly change differently between the Written and Oral groups over the study session, as indicated by the KT delivery × time interaction, F(1, 36) = 2.68, p = .110, partial 𝜂² = .069.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: There was also no statistically significant overall difference in anxiety between KT prompt groups, F(1, 36) = 1.95, p = .171, partial 𝜂² = .051, and no overall change from pre-to post-task assessment, F(1, 36) = 0.30, p = .589, partial 𝜂² = .008.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: There was also no statistically significant overall difference in anxiety between KT prompt groups, F(1, 36) = 1.95, p = .171, partial 𝜂² = .051, and no overall change from pre-to post-task assessment, F(1, 36) = 0.30, p = .589, partial 𝜂² = .008.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

papers.title: Relating smartphone ‘App-journeys’ to mental health: A novel network analysis approach
papers.summary: We found 46 t-tests and/or F-tests where effect sizes are not reported. Check these tests in the table below, and consider adding effect sizes.

findings.sentence: We found that, compared with the self-reported Most Automatic App, the self-reported Least Automatic App had a lower SRHI questionnaire score (paired t-test: t(81) = 13.189, p < 0.001, BF10 = 6.315 x 10 18 ) (Figure 4a); as well as a lower average length of time spent in an 'Appsession' (i.e., duration on App in one go before leaving) (paired t-test: t(60) = 2.306, p = 0.025, BF10 = 1.618) (Figure 4b); and was used at least once in a lower proportion of phone sessions (paired t-test: t(76) = 5.937, p < 0.001, BF10 = 159,381.300) (Figure 4c).
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Annotations represent significance of paired t-tests comparing the Most Automatic and Least Automatic App scores, with significance levels denoted as follows: * = p < 0.05, ** = p < 0.01, *** = p < 0.001, ns = not significant. (a) The Most Automatic App had a higher in-strength (t(60) = 5.134, p < 0.001, BF10 = 5,233.373), but there was no significant difference in out-strength (t(60) = -1.299, p = 0.199, BF10 = 0.311). (b) The Most Automatic App had a higher in-diversity (t(60) = 4.666, p < 0.001, BF10 = 1,074.696) but a lower out-diversity (t(60) = -3.303, p = 0.002, BF10 = 17.358). (c) The Most Automatic App had higher centrality across two separate operationalizations of node centrality: eigenvector centrality (t(60) = 5.375, p < 0.001, BF10 = 12,091.24) and coreness (t(60) = 4.365, p < 0.001, BF10 = 402.814). (d) Compared to the Most Automatic App, the Least Automatic App had a higher local clustering coefficient (paired ttest: t(60) = -4.915, p < 0.001, BF10 = 2,471.122), but a lower betweenness coefficient (paired ttest: t(60) = 3.907, p < 0.001, BF10 = 97.016).
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

papers.title: Suppressing Distractors, Enhancing Targets: Template Tuning in Ensemble Perception
papers.summary: We found 8 t-tests and/or F-tests where effect sizes are not reported. Check these tests in the table below, and consider adding effect sizes.

findings.sentence: No significant bias was observed in the Control condition, where both colors in the ensemble were novel, t(24) = 0.62, p = .539, 95% CI [-0.24, 0.46].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: However, a significant bias (after Bonferroni corrections, p < 0.0125) was found in Target Repeat when only the target color remained in the ensemble, t(24) = 3.40, p = .001, 95% CI [0.24, 0.99].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: When the distractor color was repeated in the ensemble, the response bias was significantly greater than zero, t(24) = 2.44, p = .022, 95% CI [0.06, 0.75]; however, this effect did not survive Bonferroni correction.
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: A large and robust bias was observed in the Both Repeat condition when the target and the distractor color remained in the ensemble, t(24) = 8.09, p < .001, 95% CI [1.41, 2.38] (see Figure 3A).
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Results showed that in the Control condition there was no evidence of a bias, t(29) = -0.17, p = .87, 95% CI [-0.37, 0.33].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Additionally, in the Target Repeat condition, the observed bias was modest but significant before correction, t(29) = 2.24, p = .03, 95% CI [0.04, 0.79].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: The Distractor Repeat condition did show a visibly small but not significant bias, t(29) = 1.79, p = .08, 95% CI [-0.04, 0.62].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: Finally, results revealed a significant orientation bias in the Both Repeat condition, t(29) = 6.16, p < .01, 95% CI [1.14, 2.27].
findings.note: No effect size reported with this test.

findings.sentence: For 150 ms, there was no significant difference between the Both Repeat condition and the sum of the Target Repeat and Distractor Repeat conditions, t(29) = 2.02, p = .052, 95% CI[-0.01, 1.73], Hedges's g = 0.41.
findings.note: The effect size Hedges's g = 0.41 does not fit the test. No match under tested assumptions (paired dz, independent equal-n, independent unequal-n range). Tolerance = 0.01. A no-match can occur when fewer than 2 decimal places are reported.

findings.sentence: For 500 ms, the Both Repeat condition bias was significantly larger than the sum of the Distractor Repeat and Target Repeat conditions, t(29) = 3.12, p = .004, 95% CI[0.39, 1.90], Hedges's g = 0.64.
